impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The fellow's employability and career prospects are advanced by the agreed Career Development Plan (D1.3), owned by FELLOW and SUPERVISOR and reviewed at the five re-anchored steering points (M6/M14/M18/M24/M27), together with the inter-sectoral AgroVIR placement (M25-M30). These consolidate an Agricultural Data Scientist profile spanning plant stress, Earth observation and decision support (project outcome OC5), delivering the increased research and transferable-skill set that improves prospects within academia and beyond.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The Tier 2B expected impact EI-04 as extracted concerns the spread of excellence and balanced brain circulation in widening countries through ERA Fellowships. No explicit Tier 3 project mechanism maps to this statement as written: the Tier 3 expected_impact_coverage entry keyed EI-04 addresses convergence of researcher working conditions with the European Charter for Researchers (via D1.3), which is a different impact statement. This constitutes a Tier 2B/Tier 3 discrepancy on the EI-04 identifier. To avoid substituting a generic or mismatched claim, no project output is asserted against the ERA-Fellowships/widening statement; the pathway is flagged uncovered for operator reconciliation of the expected-impact numbering.
impact_pathways.tier3_linkage_ref: impacts.json expected_impact_coverage EI-04 addresses a Charter-working-conditions statement (mapped_project_outputs D1.3), not the Tier 2B ERA/widening statement; id-vs-description conflict flagged

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The Tier 2B expected impact EI-05 as extracted concerns enhanced nuclear expertise and Euratom-supported fellowships in nuclear research areas. FIELDWISE is a non-nuclear agricultural plant-stress and decision-support project; no project mechanism can be truthfully mapped to a nuclear/Euratom impact without fabricating a claim. The Tier 3 expected_impact_coverage entry keyed EI-05 instead addresses increased R&I capacity and knowledge transfer among research organisations (via D2.1, D2.2, D3.2), a different statement from the Tier 2B EI-05 text. This is a Tier 2B/Tier 3 identifier conflict; the pathway is flagged uncovered for operator reconciliation rather than mapped to a mismatched impact.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: Strengthened R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer of the participating organisations is delivered by the primary model and model card (D2.1), the crop-transfer specification (D2.2) and the prospective transferability report (D3.2), which together constitute the reusable, uncertainty-aware, crop-configurable framework (OC2) and the quantified transfer evidence (OC3), reinforced by the two-way transfer between the fellow and the ATK/ELTE/MATE environments (Pack §1.3). The second limb of the Tier 2B EI-06 statement — feedback of research results into teaching and education — is addressed by the Pack §1.3 teaching route (guest lectures/seminars at MATE and, where possible, Plovdiv) but carries no WP deliverable; Tier 3 records this teaching limb as uncovered by a deliverable, so the pathway is mapped for the R&I-capacity limb and flagged partial for the teaching-feedback limb.

kpis.description: Career Development Plan agreed and reviewed across the project's steering points, evidencing the fellow's structured skills and career progression.
kpis.target: CDP agreed by M3 and reviewed at all five steering points (M6, M14, M18, M24, M27).
kpis.measurement_method: Documented CDP version history and dated steering-point review records against the D1.3 deliverable.

kpis.description: Transfer gap from research experiments to an independent commercial field quantified prospectively, evidencing inter-sectoral knowledge transfer into practice.
kpis.target: Prospective performance, uncertainty and any limited recalibration reported against the predefined criteria; transfer loss stated, not hidden.
kpis.measurement_method: Comparison of prospective commercial-field performance against blocked/predefined validation criteria, reported in the transferability report.

kpis.description: Non-academic operational evaluation of the MVP completed at AgroVIR, evidencing inter-sectoral placement and knowledge exchange.
kpis.target: AgroVIR assessment covers MVP inputs, usability, missing-data behaviour, decision outputs, workflow compatibility and interoperability requirements.
kpis.measurement_method: Completion and content audit of the AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment against the M25-M30 evaluation protocol.

kpis.description: Released primary model documented with calibration, uncertainty and unseen-year performance, evidencing R&I capacity and output.
kpis.target: Primary model and nonlinear benchmark (where justified) reported with calibration, uncertainty and blocked unseen-year performance in one model card.
kpis.measurement_method: Model card review confirming calibration, uncertainty quantification and blocked temporal validation results.

kpis.description: Crop-transfer specification stated, evidencing transferable, reusable R&I capacity for later crop-by-crop extension.
kpis.target: Transferable core components, crop-specific parameters, minimum validation dataset and recalibration gates enumerated for adding a new crop.
kpis.measurement_method: Audit of the crop-transfer specification for the enumerated reusable components, crop-specific parameters and recalibration gates.

activities.activity_type: Peer-reviewed publications (P1-P2, plus a third methods/application paper if the independent commercial-field dataset supports it) reporting the stress-validation methodology, model card and prospective transfer results
activities.target_audience: Plant-stress physiology, agro-informatics, remote-sensing/Earth-observation and irrigation-modelling research communities
activities.timing: M6-M30 (submission from M12; final paper contingent on D3.1/D3.2)

activities.activity_type: Open release of the primary model card (D2.1) and the crop-transfer specification (D2.2) as citable, FAIR research outputs documenting calibration, uncertainty and reusable-versus-crop-specific components
activities.target_audience: Modelling and precision-agriculture researchers and technical developers seeking to extend the framework to further irrigated high-value horticultural crops

activities.activity_type: Conference and scientific-workshop presentations of the validation framework and the quantified experiment-to-commercial-field transfer gap (D3.2)
activities.target_audience: International scientific peers in agricultural data science, plant physiology and UAV/Sentinel-2 crop monitoring

activities.activity_type: Release of the prospective commercial-field validation dataset (D3.1) with continuous environmental record and documented irrigation timing/amounts, published under FAIR principles per the Data Management Plan
activities.target_audience: Research organisations and data-reuse communities in irrigated horticulture and crop-stress modelling
activities.timing: After D3.1 delivery, subject to DMP access conditions

dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All peer-reviewed publications are made available in open access in line with Horizon Europe requirements; the released model card (D2.1) and crop-transfer specification (D2.2) are published as citable research outputs; research data (notably the prospective validation dataset D3.1) is managed under a Data Management Plan delivered within the first six months and made findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable (FAIR) to the extent that commercial-field and partner constraints allow. The distinction between the fellow's pre-existing DrR background and FIELDWISE foreground is preserved in all released materials.

activities.activity_type: Development of the web-based DrR MVP into a testable, crop-configurable decision-support tool serving field-level stress probability/class, uncertainty and an irrigation-attention output (LOW/MONITOR/HIGH/URGENT) for the validated tomato module
activities.expected_result: A tangible route from validated research to external testing, with processing tomato as the first validated crop module and reusable ingestion, uncertainty, visualisation and irrigation-attention components available for later crop modules after crop-specific validation
activities.timing: D4.1 (MVP) then D4.2 (pre-placement readiness), M25-M30 external testing

activities.activity_type: AgroVIR-led external operational evaluation and definition of the FMIS integration roadmap, specifying required interfaces, exploitation route and post-fellowship steps
activities.expected_result: Documented data, usability, interoperability and workflow requirements for future FMIS integration (D5.1) and an agreed integration path (D5.2) enabling later uptake within an operational farm-management information system

activities.activity_type: Krumatic-supported software implementation and Bulgarian farmer-facing uptake groundwork for the validated module
activities.expected_result: Software-implementation support and an inter-sectoral, cross-border (Hungary-Bulgaria) exploitation channel toward practitioner uptake
activities.timing: Software track across the project; farmer-facing uptake from MVP availability

activities.activity_type: Definition of the post-MSCA MVCRI replication route for extending the validated approach to further crops and settings
activities.expected_result: A realistic post-fellowship replication pathway toward wider reuse across irrigated high-value horticulture, without over-claiming universalisation from tomato

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: IP handling preserves the boundary between the fellow's pre-existing DrR background and the FIELDWISE foreground; the released research outputs (model card, crop-transfer specification, publications, validation data) are disseminated openly, while the DrR MVP and its crop-configurable architecture provide the exploitable foreground whose protection (e.g. controlled access, trade-secret handling of implementation detail) is defined with AgroVIR and Krumatic ahead of any FMIS integration. Economic value is not expressed as an invented EUR/ha figure; exploitation rests on the quantified operational metrics the project actually delivers.

sustainability_mechanism.description: Results persist beyond the fellowship through the crop-configurable DrR MVP architecture, in which processing tomato provides the first validated crop module and the reusable data-ingestion, uncertainty, visualisation and irrigation-attention components remain available for later crop modules after crop-specific validation. Continuity is anchored by (i) the AgroVIR FMIS integration roadmap (D5.2) that names the interfaces and post-fellowship steps required for operational uptake, (ii) Krumatic's software-implementation and Bulgarian farmer-facing channel, (iii) the defined post-MSCA MVCRI replication route toward wider reuse across irrigated high-value horticulture, and (iv) the openly released model card, crop-transfer specification and validation data that let other research organisations reuse and extend the framework. The fellow's consolidated Agricultural Data Scientist profile and Career Development Plan sustain the human capacity to carry the work forward.
